title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
claim: In a preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest of GB national demand, giving every model the same honestly timed weather forecasts cut error by about a third for a weekly-lag regression and for Chronos-2, less for Timestral-209M and TimesFM 2.5, and the models' lead over the regression largely disappears once the regression has weather.
why_relevant: Same design as our benchmark (zero-shot models with temperature against a temperature regression, forecast-regime weather), on national load a day ahead instead of zonal load a week ahead.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: Across three load datasets, Chronos-2 is the most accurate of four foundation models and four trained models when future covariates are known or well forecast, zero-shot and fine-tuned, but loses its lead as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet holds up better.
why_relevant: Tests exactly our two weather regimes (known versus forecast covariates) for Chronos-2 on electric load.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load, Chronos-2 with weather and calendar covariates is compared with task-specific deep learning models, zero-shot and after adaptation on historical data.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with temperature covariates on zonal utility load is our primary challenger on the same kind of series.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
claim: Across four PJM extreme-cold events, 90% load forecast intervals lose coverage inside the events and no conformal calibrator chosen without the target event restores it (0 of 18 pre-registered cells), while retrospective transfer evaluation overstates coverage by 12 to 21 points.
why_relevant: Pre-registered probabilistic load benchmark on our own system (PJM), day-ahead, under temperature extremes.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods
claim: On three datasets from control area to end consumer, Transformer forecasters cut short-term load error by 6.6 to 10.7% against ten established methods, and zero-shot Chronos-2 is competitive on two datasets but misses special events on the transmission-operator data.
why_relevant: A load benchmark that includes control-area load and Chronos-2 zero-shot, with a stated weakness on holidays and events.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: A live daily benchmark freezes one information set, including three weather models, half an hour before the day-ahead gate and runs baselines, boosted models and eighteen foundation models on load, price, wind and solar for six bidding zones, so they are compared with and without the same weather under the real deadline.
why_relevant: Lead-matched weather given identically to every model, including foundation models with and without covariates, is our hard rule 3 applied prospectively to zonal load.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Replication package for "Battery charging, demand statistics and the evaluation of U.S. day-ahead load forecasts"
claim: An audit of day-ahead load forecasts in EIA-930 for 49 balancing authorities (2018 to 2026) traces cases of deteriorating forecasts to how battery charging enters published load, and re-scores benchmark comparisons on that basis.
why_relevant: EIA-930 demand is our target series; the audit bears on what our 'actual load' measures and on comparing models with operator forecasts.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: For French national load, an adaptive GAM in state-space form fed with forecasts from several weather providers gives better point and probabilistic forecasts than any single provider, especially in the extreme quantiles.
why_relevant: Weather forecast error as the driver of load error, and which weather source to use, is the question of our forecast regime.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Across four foundation models and nine socially driven datasets in a zero-shot rolling evaluation, the way calendar covariates are encoded changes MASE by up to 9.9% on ordinary days and 83% on holidays within one model.
why_relevant: We feed calendar covariates to Chronos-2 and saw it get worse; this says the encoding, not the information, may be why.

title: Companion Data, Protocols and Code for Choosing Load Forecasting Methods by Horizon, History and Hour: Reserve and Imbalance Evidence from Four Grids
claim: Under a pre-specified protocol with a deviation log, rolling-origin load forecasts at horizons of 1 to 180 days plus hourly day-ahead forecasts on four grids (Jordan, Tetouan, Panama, Spain) are used to choose and combine methods by horizon and by hour.
why_relevant: A protocol-first load backtest whose horizons include the week ahead, with method choice depending on horizon.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Lead-Time-Conditioned Convex Stacked Ensemble for Medium-Term Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: A convex stacked ensemble with weights set per lead time and updated online from past losses is tested with full-year rolling weekly forecasts for Spain, France, Greece and Portugal; it is competitive with the best specialised model but does not dominate it.
why_relevant: National load forecast in weekly rolling origins over a year, close to our weekly issue schedule and horizon.
query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one university building, TimesFM 3.0 with weather and calendar covariates has the lowest error (about 43% below weekly seasonal-naive), but paired daily comparisons show no clear advantage over XGBoost, and covariates help only on holidays.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable foundation model against a tuned tree model on hourly electricity with weather, with an honest paired test.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: In two German district heating networks, zero-shot TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 with ambient temperature beat all trained baselines for hourly 24-hour heat load, under perfect weather and in a sensitivity run with archived weather forecasts.
why_relevant: Two models we can run, with temperature as a known-future covariate, in both of our weather regimes, on another hourly energy load.

title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting with Chronos-2
claim: For two non-residential buildings, giving Chronos-2 day-type indicators as past and future covariates lowers CV-RMSE from 14.6% to 10.4%, with future weather taken from archived forecasts, not observations.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with known-future covariates under forecast-regime weather; here the calendar, not the weather, carries the gain.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Across four load aggregation levels, pretrained MOIRAI and Chronos-2 beat seasonal-naive and XGBoost baselines, and rank-16 LoRA on MOIRAI Large lowers normalised MAE by a further 7.5% while training about 1% of the weights.
why_relevant: Asks whether adapting a pretrained model to load is worth it over zero-shot use, from country to building level.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: On open UK and Swiss data at three distribution aggregation levels, Chronos-2 has the lowest error in high-demand periods, 20 to 51% below LightGBM and XGBoost, while staying best or near-best overall.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 against gradient-boosted trees on load, scored on peaks, which is where our zones' errors matter most.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments: Results from a 41-day live challenge on the aggregated German transmission-grid load
claim: In a 41-day live challenge on German transmission-grid load, a deterministic open pipeline with calendar and weather covariates beat ENTSO-E's official day-ahead forecast, and small transparent local models were competitive with pretrained models of more than 100 million parameters.
why_relevant: A live (not backtest) comparison of simple auditable models with pretrained ones on system load with weather.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: Run records of a multi-horizon evaluation of national demand forecasts for Türkiye with calendar, holiday and temperature information: 759 training runs with sealed test forecasts and per-origin losses.
why_relevant: System load with temperature and holidays at several horizons, with sealed test forecasts.

title: Closed-Form Calendar Estimation in Deep Load Forecasting: per-window error files, probabilistic runs and superseded records
claim: Per-window errors and probabilistic runs of an information-controlled benchmark on eight national grids that estimates calendar effects in closed form inside deep load forecasters, with superseded records kept for audit.
why_relevant: Calendar handling in load forecasting under a logged protocol, across national grids.

title: pl-forecast-bench: a leakage-checked forecasting benchmark for the Polish power system
claim: A benchmark for Polish demand, wind, solar and price fixes data, publication-time rules, a 12-month test year and reference models from naive to zero-shot foundation models with archived ECMWF forecasts, plus tests that detect look-ahead leakage.
why_relevant: Archived lead-matched weather forecasts and as-of rules for national demand: our forecast regime as a public benchmark.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
claim: Under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, TimesFM 3 has 16% lower MASE than a pre-specified classical ensemble on post-release data, but in two sealed prospective weeks its point-forecast advantage on load, prices and river flow is not confirmed and its 80% intervals cover about 70%.
why_relevant: A post-release, leakage-aware test that includes electricity load: the same concern as our weights-after-window label.

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models
claim: In Chronos-2, t0-beta and TiRex-2, supplying eight exact copies of a covariate (for example the same temperature in two units, or nearby stations) raises the weight the model gives it where a Bayes-optimal forecaster would not change, so the number of copies acts as a hidden weight.
why_relevant: We pass temperature to Chronos-2 as a covariate; how many temperature channels we pass would change the forecast.

title: Timestral
claim: Mistral's Timestral family (5M to 209M parameters) gives probabilistic multivariate forecasts with past and known-future covariates, and the publisher says the largest model ranks first on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable open-weights model already in our runnable list (Timestral-209M through FoundationForecast); weights fall inside our scored window.

title: TimesFM-3: a zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting
claim: Google's TimesFM-3 forecasts several series with covariates in one forward pass, and the publisher says it outperforms other forecasting models across the main public benchmarks.
why_relevant: TimesFM 3.0 takes temperature natively through FoundationForecast (our TimesFM 2.5 row is univariate); weights fall inside our scored window.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: The open-weights t0 models (102M and 256M parameters) condition on past and known-future covariates; known-future covariates raise skill by 6.3 points over 30 tasks, and t0-beta is among the most accurate models on a Victoria electricity-demand benchmark.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable model in the FoundationForecast list, with a reported electricity-demand result to re-measure.

title: TimeH2O: compact time series foundation models
claim: H2O's TimeH2O-v1 (108M parameters, open weights for non-commercial use) is reported by the publisher as first of 32 on fev-bench and lowest aggregate MASE and CRPS among zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, as read on 24 October 2026.
why_relevant: Listed in our FoundationForecast wrappers as taking temperature; non-commercial licence and weights inside our scored window.

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactual truth, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 answer what-if queries on a covariate with the associational slope, and respond more confounded than a regression does.
why_relevant: Bears on how far to trust a model's response to a temperature path that differs from history.

title: Foundations without Fundamentals: Zero-Shot Blind Spots in Time Series FMs
claim: On simple unit tests such as trends, periodic signals and leading-indicator covariates, Chronos-2, Moirai and Toto often give poor zero-shot forecasts, and they under-use leading covariates on real sensor data too.
why_relevant: Temperature is a leading covariate for load; this is a direct check on whether such models use one.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: For French load forecast 1 to 48 months ahead at monthly and daily resolution with a tabular foundation model, selected economic covariates improve skill beyond weather and calendar inputs.
why_relevant: A tabular foundation model on national load with covariates, at horizons longer than ours.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: In a preregistered comparison on nine Nordic zones, zero-shot Timestral and Chronos-2 without covariates have about one point lower MAPE than SARIMA and GBM baselines on a 2025 test, but on a 14-origin post-release holdout the differences fall inside the pre-set minimum detectable effect.
why_relevant: Pre-registered, zonal, hourly, multi-day horizon, with a post-release holdout: the structure of our receipt, on a neighbouring energy series.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: Using timestamps of 128,656 weather forecast runs matched to GB auction gates, choosing the latest run issued before the gate picks a run that was not yet published on more than 99% of days for six of ten weather-model configurations.
why_relevant: Our forecast regime depends on lead-matched archived weather; this is the specific lookahead trap in that step.

title: Code and results: When Do Time Series Foundation Models Help Forecast Wind Energy Droughts? A Preregistered Evaluation
claim: A preregistered evaluation compares Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5 and Moirai-2 with climatology, model output statistics, quantile regression and a recurrent network for probabilistic forecasts of cumulative wind energy deficit in 16 regions, with weather-model covariates.
why_relevant: Pre-registered test of models we run, with numerical weather covariates, on an energy series.

title: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts
claim: TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2, zero-shot with the ensemble mean as a covariate, are compared with trained post-processing methods for 2 m temperature at 49 German stations up to 120 h ahead, to find how much training data the trained methods need to catch up.
why_relevant: Foundation models with a forecast as known-future covariate, on the temperature forecasts that feed our forecast regime.

title: U.S. utility load forecasts filed on FERC Form 714, 2006-2025: forecast errors, weather-normalized outcomes, prediction intervals and capacity decision rules
claim: Code and data evaluating 13,657 forecast and outcome pairs of peak and energy forecasts that US planning areas filed on FERC Form 714, with intervals built from past errors and a look at PJM's own forecasts.
why_relevant: Evaluates operator load forecasts including PJM's, but at planning horizons of years, not a week.

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
claim: On a hold-out made only of observations published after every model's release, pretrained forecasters win 5 of 7 groups, and what tracks their advantage is how familiar the domain is from pretraining, not seasonality of the series.
why_relevant: Our receipt reports weeks after the weights date; this says a later test window does not remove domain familiarity.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: On 7,200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol, neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominate: TimesFM-3 is never more than 1.31 times the best method's error, while automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% better on seasonal data with four or more cycles.
why_relevant: A pre-registered model-versus-classical comparison on data the model cannot have seen; short horizons, no covariates.

title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A benchmark of six foundation models on energy, traffic and financial data finds they beat statistical and supervised baselines on accuracy but trade point accuracy against calibration, with patch-based transformers poorly calibrated at long horizons.
why_relevant: Includes energy data and long horizons; relevant if the receipt adds interval scores.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A horizon-wise calibration framework applied to popular foundation models shows systematic miscalibration that pooled metrics hide, and that common recalibration methods fix only part of it.
why_relevant: Method for scoring model intervals by horizon, should the benchmark go beyond point error.

title: A survey and benchmark for household electricity forecasting
claim: A journal survey with a benchmark of about 30 models, foundation models among them, on household electricity load.
why_relevant: Electric load with foundation models in the field, at household rather than zonal level.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
claim: On daily smart-meter data for 38 homes with 48 weekly origins and lead times up to 30 days, the best of 24 configurations cut seasonal-naive error by 20 to 25%, with zero-shot Chronos-2 among the leaders.
why_relevant: Weekly origins and multi-week lead times with weather, on household rather than zonal load.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
claim: Of nine zero-shot variants from five foundation model families tested on German, Polish and Spanish day-ahead prices over 2021 to 2025, only the TabPFN models consistently beat two specialised price benchmarks, and that lead does not carry over fully to battery arbitrage value.
why_relevant: Foundation models against market-specific models on an hourly energy series, with a decision-value check.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Tabby is a 145M-parameter open model with contexts up to 8,192 points, released with its full training recipe, and is reported as competitive zero-shot on GIFT-Eval and the TIME benchmark.
why_relevant: In the FoundationForecast list as a univariate model; a long context suits a year of hourly load.

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: Timer-M1 is pretrained with explicit target, past-covariate and known-future-covariate roles and is reported first on FEV and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval among recent models.
why_relevant: A model built around known-future covariates; not in our runnable list.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: TabPFN-3.5 is reported to beat TabPFN-3 across tabular tasks and to forecast time series better through its task harness; the tabpfn-time-series package uses it by default from version 1.3.0.
why_relevant: TabPFN-TS takes temperature as a feature and is a registered (unscored) row in our protocol-v1.3; this is the newer version.

title: IBM Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2
claim: IBM reports PatchTST-FM-r2 at a geometric-mean CRPS of 0.467 on GIFT-Eval, just behind TimesFM-3 and first among permissively licensed models, with a documented pretraining corpus that excludes the benchmark's data.
why_relevant: PatchTSTFM is in the FoundationForecast list as a univariate model, with a permissive licence.

title: SAP-RPT-TS: SAP's new Time Series Foundation Model
claim: SAP describes SAP-RPT-TS as a zero-shot model of about 28M parameters with past and future covariates and horizons up to 1,024 steps, run on SAP AI Core or in SAP HANA Cloud.
why_relevant: Covariate-capable and CPU-friendly by the publisher's account, but offered through SAP services, so probably not runnable by us.

title: A controlled benchmark of temporal dependence for day-ahead electricity-demand discrepancies in Great Britain
claim: A retrospective benchmark on 364 ordinary days of 2024 compares independent, Gaussian-copula and empirical ensembles of the gap between day-ahead demand forecasts and outturn in Great Britain, keeping adverse and inconclusive findings.
why_relevant: About the error structure of operator day-ahead demand forecasts, not a competing forecaster.

title: Online Conditional Vine Copulas: Forecasting Electricity Demand
claim: An online vine copula with covariate-dependent parameters forecasts the joint distribution of net demand in five GB regions better than unconditional Gaussian and vine benchmarks.
why_relevant: Regional (multi-zone) demand with covariates, as a joint distribution; a different question from our point forecasts.

title: Ranking reliability in building level day ahead load forecasting: analysis code
claim: With sixteen forecasters from seasonal naive to pretrained models, the code measures how the length of the evaluation window and the number of models compared change how reliable a ranking is, on a ten-origin and a 238-origin protocol.
why_relevant: Our leaderboard ranks models on 45 to 52 origins; this measures how stable such rankings are.

title: Replication data and code for: What is "load"? Grid batteries, rooftop solar and long-term hourly forecasting in California
claim: For California's zonal hourly load, the study asks what published load measures once battery charging and rooftop solar are accounted for, and tests a bottom-up forecast on stable load layers against official long-term hourly benchmarks.
why_relevant: Zonal hourly load and what the published series contains, at long-term horizons.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting
claim: A two-stage method models weather response, load history and residuals for feeder power, then calibrates only the extreme quantiles against a simple anchor forecast.
why_relevant: Probabilistic load with weather at feeder level; method paper, no pretrained model.

title: From Shared Demand Patterns to Local Uncertainty: Probabilistic Load Forecasting by Mixing Compact Adaptations
claim: A shared forecasting model with a small bank of low-dimensional adaptations mixed per load improves deterministic and probabilistic accuracy on 590 customer and transformer load profiles.
why_relevant: Load forecasting at customer level; far from zonal week-ahead.

title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
claim: A context-aware agent reads notices, weather alerts and event schedules and decides whether to forecast the whole horizon or split it where event effects change.
why_relevant: Load forecasting driven by event text, not a covariate-fed pretrained forecaster we could run.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark
